messages:
Frank (CEO): Quick Q&A: during the all-hands we asked for a short, evidence-backed "why we win / why we lose" for the board packet. Can we capture the top asks and which would move the needle most?

Hannah (PM): From recent win/loss interviews and customer calls: Wins: 1) Dedicated capacity + SLA, 2) transparent committed pricing for large throughput, 3) clear privacy/KMS commitments. Losses: 1) customers comparing unit economics to self-host, 2) absence of an on-prem/offline option for regulated verticals, 3) UX gaps: model pinning & rollback.

Noah (VP Sales): Sales color: the single clearest blocker for 2 enterprise deals last quarter was "must run in customer datacenter". If we can offer a minimally supported on-prem bundle those deals would have closed. For other deals, having a perf/throughput one-pager with real numbers short-circuits a lot of procurement back-and-forth.

Jia (Product): Product mitigation ideas: short-term: add "pin model" and "revert" in Console + expose model-id in logs. Medium-term: a hardened air-gapped runtime image with KMS hooks. Need security and support plan. I'll write a proposal.

Sam (Support): From tickets and renewals: biggest churn drivers are repeated latency variance at peaks and unexpected quality drops after model swaps. We recommend a standard "rollback playbook" and sample runbook for customers. Also want per-request model id surfaced in tracing.

Ravi (Data): Small data preview from CRM tags since 2025-09-01: sla_commit=10, need_onprem=7, pin_model=9. I'll produce a CSV mapping lost reasons to ARR impact and a conservative "avoidable churn" estimate.

Hannah (PM): Leadership asks: if we could deliver one thing in 90 days that reduces avoidable churn most, what is it? My suggestion: on-prem/offline bundle + audit logs for regulated finance/health. Secondary: model pin/rollback for retention. Which should be prioritized depends on near-term pipeline.

Frank (CEO): If Sales can point to 2-3 live opportunities that require on-prem, we'll consider fast-tracking it. Otherwise focus on pin/rollback which helps many customers.

Noah (VP Sales): I'll surface two anonymized RFP lines and the deal IDs by EOD tomorrow.

Jia (Product): I'll draft the pin/rollback RFC and include estimated effort and minimal acceptance criteria (automated fallback, telemetry, Console toggle). Due Fri.

Sam (Support): I'll upload three anonymized renewal notes showing escalation language and recommend copy for sales rebuttals.

ops-bot: created doc playbooks/win-loss/board-ready-summary by @Hannah

Hannah (PM): Action items recap: Noah -> RFPs/deals (Tue), Jia -> RFC for pin/rollback (Fri), Ravi -> avoidable-churn model + CSV (Tue), Sam -> support snippets (Wed). Owners acknowledged?

Noah (VP Sales): Acknowledged.

Jia (Product): Acknowledged.

Ravi (Data): Acknowledged.

Sam (Support): Acknowledged.

Frank (CEO): Thanks team. Hannah, please synthesize a one-page for the board with the avoidable-churn number and the proposed 90-day lift.

Hannah (PM): Will do ":memo:". Thanks everyone!
